citation.title: Model-based electron density profile estimation and control, applied to ITER
citation.authors: T. O. S. J. Bosman, M. van Berkel, M. R. de Baar
citation.venue: Journal of Physics Communications (per record hint; extracted text is the arXiv preprint marked 'submitted to')
citation.doi_or_arxiv: arXiv:2110.14975; DOI 10.1088/2399-6528/ac3547 per record hint, not confirmed in the extracted text

topic: Electron density profile state estimation (EKF with a control-oriented transport model and synthetic Thomson scattering) and MPC with pellets for ITER, in simulation only
own_question: Can synthetic Thomson-scattering data within an EKF observer reconstruct the ITER ne profile, and can MPC track a reference while respecting Greenwald and impurity-transport gradient constraints?
actual_method_and_evidence: RAPDENS B-spline model with EKF and covariance tuning. Synthetic Gaussian-noise Thomson-scattering data derived from one integrated-modelling ITER scenario (#134173), with deliberate plant-observer mismatch. Reported estimation error is about 10% in ramp-up and about 2% in flat-top. A linear disturbance-augmented MPC with Ts=3 ms was simulated against RAPDENS only. No experimental data and no real-time timing measurements.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Electron density from Thomson scattering; no ion or impurity temperature and no CES. The 3 ms MPC sample time is a design choice, not a measured computation time.
validation_if_relevant: Simulation only: synthetic measurements from one modelled discharge, no held-out data, and systematic errors excluded.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it as evidence for CES or impurity-Ti nowcasting.
Do not cite it as achieved real-time performance or a demonstrated ITER result.
Do not treat it as representative of all prior work.
Do not equate its electron-density state estimation with our current-report nowcasting.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Different quantity and diagnostic, and validation is simulation only. At most it could serve as an optional generic example of model-based profile observers, which our framing does not need.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
